migration.description: Add pauseable approval revision history beside the stable-ID current CAS projection.
migration.release_unit_description: Phase-one execution-domain candidate following migration 00011; history transfer and writer cutover are explicit operations outside startup Goose migration.

compatibility_assessment.reason: Public approval IDs, response fields, limits, authorization and exact resolution CAS remain stable. The additive history table preserves only revisions actually observed by the durable projection and the opaque cursor remains Run-bound and versioned.

durable_state.description: The current approval projection remains the write-side CAS row keyed by stable native request ID. History rows are keyed by (id, revision), retain raw context and requested-event identity, and remain readable across execution generations.
durable_state.storage_implementation: PostgreSQL tables and the capture/writer triggers are created by embedded Goose migration 00012. Checkpoint, lease, dirty-row and phase state are durable in PostgreSQL. Historical transfer, concurrent indexes and final cutover are executed by the explicit approval-history migrator.

source_compatibility_range.from_program_versions: Phase-one approval-history candidate containing migrations 00009 through 00011.
source_compatibility_range.to_program_version: Phase-one stable-ID approval revision-history candidate after explicit cutover_complete.
source_compatibility_range.compatibility_boundary: Projection-only writers remain supported while capture is active. They are fenced only after the bounded cutover commits; after the first new history write, switchback requires a history-capable candidate.

ddl_structural_changes.description: Create the history table, durable migration state, dirty-row queue, capture function, writer-guard function and short-lived capture trigger. No projection table lock is held across data work.
Build the Run cursor and requested-event indexes with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY after validation. Invalid or incomplete indexes are detected and repaired forward.
Under a bounded execution_approvals SHARE lock, reconcile only the remaining dirty IDs within strict row/work budgets, install the writer guard, remove capture and commit cutover_complete.

dml_changes.description: While capture is active, every supported projection insert or update writes or reconciles the same durable history snapshot and queues its ID in the same transaction. Approval deletion is rejected because the current product has no supported deletion semantics.
Run a bounded dirty-row pre-drain and a non-blocking projection/history consistency audit outside the final writer lock. A dirty queue that exceeds its budget leaves capture and old mode active.

historical_data_backfill_or_transformati.description: Copy one exact current snapshot per existing execution_approvals row in bounded keyset batches. The checkpoint and batch writes commit together; missing older revisions are not synthesized.

For a previously applied atomic 00012 preview state, recognize the original table, valid indexes and revision-history writer guard, validate projection/history equality and register cutover_complete without changing Goose history or invoking Down.

progress_signals: The phase row exposes checkpoint_id, scanned/copied counts, dirty reconciliation count, lease ownership, expiry and last error.
Each backfill batch is a committed keyset transaction; cancel or process exit leaves the prior checkpoint recoverable and safe to re-enter.
The capture trigger makes concurrent projection-only writes visible in history and the dirty queue without a history-volume table lock.
Concurrent indexes are ready only when pg_index reports both indisvalid and indisready and the definition matches the required keyset or partial index.
Readiness is admitted only at cutover_complete with both indexes, the enabled writer guard and an empty dirty queue; startup does not repeat a full history scan.
pause_points: After the structural Goose migration commits and before the explicit transfer operation.
After any committed backfill batch or pre-drain batch.
Before and after concurrent index construction.
Before final cutover lock acquisition; lock_timeout, statement_timeout, final row budget and final work budget are mandatory.
A timeout, oversized dirty queue or validation failure rolls back cutover and retains capture plus the old projection mode.

recovery.faulty_release_recovery: A fresh unpublished 00012 may be reworked before release. A previously applied atomic 00012 is adopted only through explicit recognition and forward state registration. Interrupted staged work resumes from durable phase/checkpoint; unrecognized layouts fail closed.

required_test_evidence: Goose migration 00012 creates only structural state and capture; startup migration does not copy approval rows, build historical indexes or install the final writer guard.
Real PostgreSQL backfill preserves raw context bytes, requested_event_id, current status and timestamps, and does not invent discarded revisions.
Old projection-only insert/update transactions concurrent with backfill are captured atomically, and capture failures roll back the projection write.
Pause, cancellation, process restart and re-entry preserve checkpoint monotonicity and do not duplicate or lose history rows.
Concurrent index failure leaves no falsely ready index; invalid or incomplete index state is repaired forward.
A dirty queue exceeding the pre-drain or final cutover budget leaves old mode and capture active without holding an unbounded SHARE lock.
The exact previously applied atomic 00012 layout is adopted, while a near-miss layout is rejected without changing Goose history.
Server and Worker approval writers fail closed before cutover_complete, and readiness uses durable phase/index/guard facts without a startup full-table consistency scan.
